flagship.title: Alder, on the smaller lake
flagship.standfirst: A compact woodland circuit around Park Lake, with a picnic rather than a long hike as the shape of the day.
flagship.why_this_week: Tuesday’s eastern woodland choice is a little longer on foot; this western alternative deliberately makes less of the walking and more of a leisurely picnic. Alder is an easy 0.8-mile loop beside Park Lake, not the longer Lake Shore circuit or Itusi bike network. Follow the white diamonds from the visitor-center area, leaving Rupert time to sniff. It is a long drive for a small walk, so choose it for an unhurried park day rather than a mileage goal. Bring all drinking water for both of you: an old official boil-water notice remains online and its rescission has not been verified. No boat rental, swimming or visitor-center entry for Rupert is part of the plan. The publication-day NWS forecast is sunny in the mid-60s for both weekend days, with colder nights. Treat that as a dated outlook and check again before the long drive.
flagship.headline_condition: Sunny outlook; bring your own water

panels.label: The little lake circuit
panels.text: Alder is an easy 0.8-mile loop with white-diamond blazes. Start at the visitor-center parking area; do not substitute the longer Lake Shore or bike trails.

panels.label: Bring all your water
panels.text: An official July 2023 boil-water notice still says it remains in effect until updated. No rescission was verified; use water carried from home for you and Rupert rather than assuming park taps are safe.

artwork.brief: Restrained environmental mode after actual latest-six visual review: navy play-bow, cream waterside recline, layered autumn seated portrait, oxblood frontal walk, ochre ball head and cream frontal rest. Recent modes are mixed; choose a standing alert Rupert in a wind-brushed meadow with seedhead grasses and a low distant hedgerow, cream sky and olive/ochre ground. Three-quarter front body, head turned left, athletic proportions, slim tapered tail; fine cream engraving and mustard collar. Unlike the flat-field standing Plate006, vary spatial layering, foreground grass overlap, subject angle and scale; no mountains, water, sun or duplicate trees/pose from woodland010. Independent character print, not a literal destination/activity illustration. Preserve Plate006 likeness, print texture and restrained palette; deliberate negative space rather than decorative complexity.

local_trail.title: A small leg-stretch
local_trail.line: Walk the beginning of Alder and turn back before it becomes a full circuit if Rupert has had enough. Bring your own water; stay away from the swim beach.

conditions.trail_note: Follow Alder’s white diamonds beside Park Lake. Wet leaves and roots can still be slippery despite the sunny forecast; turn back at unsafe obstacles rather than detouring. Bring all drinking water, stay off the swim beach, and finish in daylight before the 6 p.m. day-use closure.

practical.best_window: Saturday or Sunday in full daylight, after checking the latest forecast and trail status. Allow time for the long drive, a short walk and an optional picnic; finish before dark and the 6 p.m. day-use closure. Bring a warm layer for the cooler morning.
practical.fees: Free ordinary day use; camping, permits, rentals and facility reservations are separate.
